options.text: The successful jump sizes are $1$, $2$, $3$ and $6$.
Jump sizes $1$, $2$, $3$, $6$ and $15$ all work — including $15$, which reaches $30$ only.
Every common factor of $18$ and $30$ is a successful jump size, so $1$, $2$, $3$ and $6$ work.
The successful jump sizes are the common multiples of $18$ and $30$.

stem:
Tushar marks two treasure numbers, $18$ and $30$, on a number strip. He may use only one jump size, repeated from $0$, and that jump size must land exactly on both numbers.

One or more options may be correct. Which two claims correctly name the successful jump sizes?

teacher.key_rationale: Common factors of 18 and 30 are 1,2,3,6. Including 15 reaches only 30; listing common multiples confuses factors with multiples.
